sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Wyoming, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Monday, November 2Passed

You may ask any time during 2026 except on Election Day itself, so the last day is Monday, November 2, 2026. (Rule: any time in the calendar year of the election, but not on the day of the election.) A ballot mailed to you can take up to 7 days to arrive within the county, and longer outside it, so a late request may not leave time to mail it back. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received in your county clerk's office by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot that arrives later is not counted, even if it was mailed earlier; there is no postmark rule. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Wyoming’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Wyoming or in another state? What Wyoming says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered Wyoming voter may ask for an absentee ballot; you do not have to say why. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By phone. Call your county clerk. Give your full name, date of birth, your Wyoming home address, the address where the ballot should be mailed, and which election you want a ballot for. Requests go to your own county clerk; the Secretary of State lists every county clerk's phone and e-mail. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Print and fill out the absentee ballot request form and mail it to your county clerk. Open it (official page)
  • By e-mail. E-mail your county clerk with "Absentee Ballot Request" in the subject line and the same information. (official page)
  • In person. Ask at your county clerk's office. If you pick up the ballot in person, you must show an acceptable ID. (the law)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the envelope provided to your county clerk's office. The Secretary of State says mail within the county may take up to 7 days, and longer from outside the county. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it, in the signed envelope, to your county clerk's office by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign and date the sworn statement printed on the back of the inner ballot envelope, then seal your ballot inside it. No witness or notary is needed for the ballot. The Secretary of State says a voter who mails in an absentee ballot does not need to add any ID, with one exception: if you registered by mail and this is your first federal election, put a copy of a photo ID or a document showing your name and home address in the envelope with your ballot. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Wyoming’s own site

The Secretary of State says to contact your county clerk for the status of your ballot. For military and overseas voters, the Secretary of State posts a list showing when each county received their general election ballot. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 6, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

Absentee voting in person at your county clerk's office runs from Tuesday, October 6 through Monday, November 2, 2026 (from 28 days before the election to the day before). (official page)

Students

At school in Wyoming, away from home

The state's pages do not speak to students separately. Its general rule, in Wyoming law, is that you do not gain or lose a residence just by being a student, and that your residence is where you actually live and mean to return to when you are away. You may register only in the precinct where you are a resident. A student who stays registered at home can ask that county's clerk for an absentee ballot. If you move within Wyoming, the Secretary of State says you need to tell the county clerk. The Secretary of State accepts a photo ID card from the University of Wyoming, a Wyoming community college or a Wyoming public school, or a school housing verification form dated within 90 days, when you register. (the law)

At school in another state, with Wyoming as home

The state's pages do not speak to students separately. Its general rule, in Wyoming law, is that you do not lose your Wyoming residence by leaving for another state for a while if you mean to come back and have not registered to vote in that other state. A Wyoming voter studying out of state can ask their county clerk for an absentee ballot by phone, mail or e-mail and have it mailed to their school address. The ballot must reach the county clerk by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)

Military and overseas

Service members, their families and U.S. citizens living abroad can ask their county clerk for a ballot by phone, e-mail, fax or mail, or use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), which also works as a temporary registration (the Secretary of State says to send in the Wyoming registration form too to stay registered). Ballots for the general election were sent starting September 18, 2026 (45 days before the election). The voted ballot must reach the county clerk by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. If your ballot has not come by 3 weeks before the election, the Secretary of State suggests the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot from FVAP. (official page)

Wyoming in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Wyoming does not mail a ballot to every voter: you must ask your county clerk for one.
  • Wyoming law asks for acceptable ID when you pick up an absentee ballot in person or vote at an absentee polling place, and lets counties open extra absentee polling places; ask your county clerk.
  • There is no postmark rule. A mailed ballot counts only if it is in the county clerk's office by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day, and the Secretary of State says mail can take a week or more.
  • The Secretary of State's pages name two ways to return a ballot: by mail or in person at the county clerk's office. They do not mention drop boxes; ask your county clerk if any are offered.
  • Not registered yet? Wyoming lets you register and vote at the same time during absentee voting at the county clerk's office or at your polling place on Election Day, with proof of identity, U.S. citizenship and Wyoming residence.
  • If you marked your ballot but have not sent it in and want to change your vote, you may destroy it and ask your county clerk for a replacement, or vote in person. Once the clerk receives it, it cannot be changed.
